questions.prompt: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Which statement is correct?
options: Its velocity changes direction continuously but its speed is constant
Both velocity and speed are constant
questions.explanation: Uniform circular motion: the speed (magnitude of velocity) is constant but the direction of velocity is continuously changing — so velocity is NOT constant. The change in velocity gives a non-zero centripetal acceleration directed toward the centre.

questions.prompt: The centripetal acceleration of a particle moving in a circle of radius r with speed v is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration aᶜ = v² / r, directed toward the centre of the circle. Equivalently, aᶜ = ω²r where ω is the angular velocity.
